name: Colombian Spanish (Coastal)
notes: Colombian coastal (costeño — Cartagena, Barranquilla, Santa Marta). Full Caribbean phonology: aspiration, [ŋ], liquid neutralisation, -d deletion. Phonologically divergent from Bogotá highland. WORD-FINAL /n/ IS VELAR [ŋ] before a pause, a vowel, a glide or a velar, and takes the place of a following consonant by the es-ES rules ES_EXT_FINAL_N_LABIAL and ES_EXT_FINAL_N_CORONAL (un peso [um ˈpeso], en la [en la]). Lipski (2011, p. 7): «Velarization of phrase-final /n/ is the rule in Galicia and parts of Asturias, Extremadura, Andalusia, the Canary Islands, all Caribbean and Central American dialects, along the Pacific coast of Colombia, Peru, and Ecuador, and sporadically in the Andean highlands. Word-final prevocalic nasals are typically also velarized in these dialects»; the Caribbean region of the same overview (p. 3, list (2)) includes the Caribbean coast of Colombia.

sources.notes: READ (geo.pdf). Reproduces the Lipski (1994) geographical dialect-zone classification of Latin American Spanish (list (2)): Mexican/SW-US; Caribbean; Guatemala-Yucatan-Costa Rica; El Salvador-Honduras-Nicaragua; interior Colombia + highland Venezuela; Pacific coast Colombia/Ecuador/Peru; Andean (Ecuador/Peru/Bolivia/NW-Argentina/NE-Chile); Chile; Paraguay/NE-Argentina/E-Bolivia; Argentina/Uruguay. Used here to enumerate the regional zones and p. 7 for the velar word-final /n/.

location.notes: Barranquilla — a representative city of the Colombian Caribbean coast (with Cartagena and Santa Marta). [Wikidata Q62823 P625]

allophone_rules.notes: Lowland coda /s/ lenition (aspiration tier of Lipski's 1994 cline): syllable-final /s/ (from ⟨s⟩ and seseante ⟨z⟩) weakens to the glottal aspirate [h] (esta=[ˈehta], los=[loh], diez=[djeh]).
